summary: Energy management in cities is a significant challenge. CityLearn addresses this issue by providing a standardized environment for evaluating Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents in building energy coordination and demand response. This facilitates comparison of algorithm performance, ultimately contributing to more efficient energy use in urban areas. The project focuses on energy models of buildings and distributed energy resources, enabling the evaluation of RL agents in a virtual district setting. By simplifying the analysis of results from smart energy communities, CityLearn supports the development of more effective energy management strategies. This, in turn, can lead to reduced energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions in cities.
